policy: Review every closed candidate set. Select only when ASV wording or an explicit mapped textual note distinguishes a reading; otherwise mark underdetermined and retain the base fallback. The base candidate is the SBLGNT reading.

decisions.evidence: Word-order variant only (kappa-alpha-rho-pi-on plerona vs plerona karpon); ASV 'more fruit' renders either order identically and no note is mapped here.
Present vs aorist subjunctive of meno; ASV 'except it abide in the vine' carries no aspectual marking that would distinguish menei from meinei.
Present vs aorist subjunctive of meno; ASV 'except ye abide in me' is aspectually neutral in English and no note is mapped here.
Present vs aorist subjunctive of meno; ASV 'If a man abide not in me' does not distinguish the two subjunctive forms.
ASV renders an imperative, 'ask whatsoever ye will, and it shall be done unto you', matching aorist imperative aitesasthe; the RP future indicative aitesesthe would yield 'ye shall ask'.

ASV text reads 'and so shall ye be my disciples', a future indicative matching genesesthe, and the mapped textual_variant note assigns the subjunctive rendering ('and be my disciples') to 'many ancient authorities' instead.
Word-order variant only (humas egapesa vs egapesa humas); ASV 'have loved you' renders either order and no note is mapped here.
ASV reads 'my Father's commandments', rendering the possessive mou that the base has (tas entolas tou patros mou); the WH reading tou patros tas entolas has no mou to support 'my'.
ASV reads 'that my joy may be in you', the copula rendering e; the RP meinei would give 'may abide/remain in you', which the ASV reserves for meno elsewhere in this chapter.

ASV 'the things which I command you' is plural, excluding the singular relative ho (r01), but does not distinguish plural ha from hosa, since ASV renders both with a plain plural relative here and no note is mapped.
Word-order variant only (lego humas vs humas lego); ASV 'do I call you servants' renders either order and the mapped notes are greek_gloss on 'servants', not textual.
ASV reads 'before it hated you', rendering the genitive of comparison humon; without humon the clause would read simply 'hath hated me first'.
eis humas and the simple dative humin both render as 'unto you'; ASV wording does not distinguish the construction and no note is mapped here.
eichosan and eichon are alternative forms of the same imperfect; ASV 'they had not had sin' renders either identically.
ASV reads 'which none other did', a simple past matching the aorist epoiesen; the RP perfect pepoieken would be rendered 'hath done' in the ASV's consistent handling of the Greek perfect.
eichosan and eichon are alternative forms of the same imperfect; ASV 'they had not had sin' renders either identically.
Word-order variant only; ASV 'that is written in their law' renders either order and the single mapped note is a cross-reference to Ps. 35:19; 69:4.

ASV opens the verse 'But when the Comforter is come'; the adversative 'But' renders the connective de, which the base text lacks. The two mapped notes are alternative_rendering on 'Comforter' and 'proceedeth' and do not bear on this unit.
